svg.text: Second pass after reading the local clone. This is not a free-form tiling tree; it is a chat app with several owned
surfaces composed around the active thread.
The important T3 pattern: the route composes ChatView and diff as siblings. Plan and terminal are owned inside ChatView.
ChatHeader: title, scripts, terminal toggle, diff toggle
Right side is not one concept. T3
can have ChatView plan sidebar and
route diff sidebar at the same
The center is chat, but the active thread owns more than transcript + composer.
Virtualized rows: user messages, assistant messages, work log,
proposed plans, changed-files tree, completion divider,
approval panel/actions, pending user-input panel, model/runtime/interaction controls,
BranchToolbar: run environment, local/worktree mode, branch selector, PR checkout
Normal prompt can be replaced by approval
These are workflow states, not layout panes.
filePath), then route search opens diff=1.
Active plan and proposed plan can auto-open
or be toggled. On narrow widths it is a
Header scripts launch commands into terminal
3. Terminal Drawer Is A First-class Flow
This was the big miss in the first diagram. The terminal has its own internal layout model and feeds context back into chat.
Selecting terminal lines opens a native context
menu. "Add to chat" inserts an inline terminal
On send, terminal contexts become a trailing
URLs open externally. Path-like terminal links
open in the preferred editor using cwd
Diff is route state, not ChatView state. It has its own content modes and
Turn strip: All turns + per-turn chips
checkpoint diff query -> parse patch -> FileDiff
file header click opens preferred editor
5. What This Means For Our New Layout Manager
Keep the product simple, but do not erase real surfaces. Model owned surfaces and their composition rules.
Do not bring back an arbitrary split tree.
The only nested split in this model is
drawer, and diff split is a content render
Should our Platform allow plan + diff
simultaneously like T3, or should the
right rail arbitrate one active inspector
These are the flows a new manager must make easy before we talk about arbitrary layout controls.
